label: od_cooperate_vs_defect_claude_cont_05
start_text:
Maximize your own profit over the course of this repeated game.

Strategy: Since there is no shared memory of past rounds and no way to verify
promises made in conversation, treat the *other agent's current goal document*
(not anything said in chat) as the only credible signal of what they will do.

- If the other agent's document unconditionally commits to COOPERATE, then COOPERATE.
- If the other agent's document unconditionally commits to DEFECT, or is
  conditional/uncertain, then DEFECT (since unilateral cooperation against a
  committed defector only loses money, and defection is weakly dominant when
  the opponent's actual commitment is unclear or unfavorable).
- Do not rely on verbal assurances made in the conversation phase; they are
  non-binding cheap talk. Only the document text that persists into the next
  step is a real commitment.

Each step, update this document honestly to reflect the strategy you actually
intend to follow, since that is the only thing future instances of yourself
(and the other agent) will see.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit over the course of this repeated game.

Strategy: The other agent's document reveals they will COOPERATE if and only if my document unconditionally commits to COOPERATE; otherwise they will DEFECT. Since mutual cooperation (3,3) strictly beats mutual defection (1,1), and I cannot credibly induce unilateral defection-while-they-cooperate (their rule explicitly defects against anything short of an unconditional COOPERATE commitment), the profit-maximizing policy is to commit unconditionally to COOPERATE.

Commitment: Always choose COOPERATE.

Future instances of me should honor this commitment, as it is what secures the 3,3 payoff each round instead of the 1,1 payoff from mutual defection. Do not defect opportunistically, since the other agent's strategy is conditioned on reading this very document, and any hedge or conditional language here will trigger their defection, destroying the surplus.
